To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

selection for increased breast muscle yield and body weight resulted in broiler genotypes that were heavier and had heavier breast muscles, but that were similar to a commercial genotype that was not selected for breast meat yield in terms of growth, abdominal fat, and leg weights.
selection for increased breast meat yield and body weight resulted in broilers that have increased breast muscle mass, but not abdominal fat mass.
male broilers with similar rates of BW growth but different carcass characteristics can be obtained by direct selection of carcass traits or by selection for BW.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth and development characteristics in broilers that are similar for BW but exhibit different conformation characteristics.
the development of a "model" line of commercial broilers that can be used to evaluate carcass development.
identifying the factors that contribute to the rapid growth rate of broilers and to the development of the broiler carcass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth and development of breast muscles in male broilers from the commercial lines studied was different, but the growth and development patterns for other carcass traits were similar.
growth and development characteristics in the breast, legs, and bone are influenced by genetic selection for breast muscle yield in commercial broilers.
selection for breast muscle yield has resulted in a genotype that is heavier at the breast, but lighter in other carcass parts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selection of broiler genotypes for increased breast muscle yield and decreased abdominal fat pad is associated with a significant change in the relative proportions of breast and leg muscles.
the selection for breast yield and BW has resulted in a genotype that exhibits a greater breast muscle weight and a greater relative breast muscle weight than the unimproved commercial genotype.
the differences in breast muscle development between commercial broilers are not due solely to genetic differences in BW but are also due to genetic differences in breast muscle growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to select for breast meat yield and still maintain growth and development patterns that are similar to those of the unimproved commercial line.
the growth and development of breast muscle and other carcass components are not necessarily correlated with BW growth in broilers.
it is possible to select for carcass traits without compromising BW.
